- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for consecutive positive sentiment.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (forecast > true by >10%) — apply downward correction if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Overshoot in early forecast horizon (days 1–7) — reduce first 3–5 days’ forecast by 3–8% if sentiment is high or volatile.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops below 0.3 after 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- Avoid overconfidence in high-sentiment periods — if sentiment > 0.8 for 3+ consecutive days, cap forecast increase at +5% above prior period.
- Correct for “sentiment echo” — if sentiment peaks and forecast rises sharply, reduce forecast by 5–10% if true outcome is below 10% of forecast range.
